subject: Site control & licensing flow for on-prem deployment - EdgeHealth
messages:
From: Susan Bell <susan.bell@edgehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgehealth.com>, procurement@edgehealth.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify on-prem licensing + evidence path (EdgeHealth)

Hi Sean / Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we get legal engaged on redlines, Procurement and Infrastructure have a couple of gating questions about the on-prem / VPC deployment model in the Order Form attached. Quick summary of asks below — can you confirm what you can provide and how?

1) Licensing boundary: our security team needs to confirm whether the license covers only the service container image and runtime, or also includes any derivative artifacts (e.g., compiled model weights, quantized artifacts). We need explicit wording to present to counsel.

2) Operator access & audits: we will likely ask for an evidence path during renewal/termination windows. Do you support:
   - read-only forensic snapshot export?
   - time-limited remote session for witness testing?
   - signed custody attestation from an operator?

3) Escrow-like contingency: if we require a fallback for critical care workloads, what options do you offer short of full source escrow? Would a sealed snapshot + independent witness suffice?

4) Timeline: procurement would like a short note we can include in the order form that describes the expected lead time for producing evidence (e.g., 2 weeks after request).

Attached: OrderForm_EdgeHealth_v2.pdf (current draft).

Can we get preliminary answers by Monday so our counsel has something to work from? Happy to discuss on a quick call.

Best,
Susan Bell
Head of Procurement
EdgeHealth

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Bell <susan.bell@edgehealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify on-prem licensing + evidence path (EdgeHealth)

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list. Rachel / Hannah / Marissa from Legal & Delivery are looped so we can give you specific language. High-level answers to start: 

• Licensing boundary: we typically license the runtime and the model binaries necessary to run the service as deployed. We do not transfer model training data or training checkpoints. We can add explicit language that limits licensed artifacts to "serving binaries, optimized weights, and runtime images required for inference".

• Operator access & audits: we can support a combination of (a) sealed forensic snapshot export (read-only) with integrity manifest, (b) time-limited remote witness sessions under a signed NDA, and (c) a signed operator custody attestation. Each option has operational lead time — will ask Hannah to enumerate.

• Contingency path (escrow-like): we offer a sealed snapshot deposit workflow (not source escrow) plus an independent witnessing option. We should propose a contractual exhibit that describes the steps, approvals, and acceptance tests.

• Timeline: provisional lead times below — Rachel / Hannah please confirm for legal wording: snapshot export ~10 business days; witness session scheduling 2–3 weeks; custody affidavit 3–5 business days after operator signoff.

Next steps: Rachel, can you draft suggested contract language for: (1) license boundary sentence, (2) an Exhibit: Evidence & Snapshot Procedure, (3) a short SLA clause for evidence delivery timelines (to include exceptions)? Susan / Tom — if you can confirm which contingency model you prefer (sealed snapshot vs witness), we’ll tailor the draft.

I’ll also attach a starter redline for MSA addendum for your counsel to review.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of North America Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed contract language + ops notes for EdgeHealth

Team — drafting notes below to convert Sean's bullets into redline-ready language. Please reply with edits by EOD Monday.

1) License scope (proposed sentence for MSA/Order Form):
   "Provider grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use Provider's runtime images, compiled inference artifacts (including optimized or quantized model weights), and associated configuration files solely for Customer's internal inference workloads within their designated on-prem/VPC environment. Provider explicitly does not license training datasets, training checkpoints, or development source code."

   Rationale: explicit inclusion of "quantized model weights" avoids procurement ambiguity.

2) Exhibit: Evidence & Snapshot Procedure (outline):
   - Requesting party files formal evidence request via secure portal (HubSpot ticket id appended).
   - Provider prepares a sealed, read-only snapshot (hash-signed) of the deployed runtime image + inference artifacts.
   - Snapshot delivered to Customer's secure S3 bucket or physically transferred under agreed transfer protocol.
   - Independent witnessing may be requested; witness session scheduled within 15 business days of request (subject to mutual availability).
   - Provider produces an Operator Custody Attestation signed by on-call operator within 5 business days of snapshot creation.

3) Contingency / fallback (contract exhibit options):
   Option A — Sealed Snapshot Deposit: Provider deposits snapshot with mutually agreed third-party custodian. Custodian releases snapshot only upon documented termination events.
   Option B — Witnessed Transfer: Provider performs a witnessed, time-boxed transfer to Customer with acceptance tests run during session.

4) Timeline SLA suggestions:
   - Snapshot export: 10 business days (standard)
   - Witness session: scheduled within 15 business days
   - Custody attestation: 5 business days after snapshot creation

5) Risks / carveouts to include in the addendum:
   - No transfer of model training data or developer source code.
   - Third-party custodian costs may be charged to Customer (to be specified in Order Form).
   - Availability windows and blackout periods (maintenance) can affect lead times.

Attachments: I will produce a redline PDF for Sean to send to EdgeHealth showing the license sentence + Exhibit outline.

Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Susan / Tom — thanks for the quick turn. Per below, legal and delivery have drafted the suggested language and process. High-level summary and attachments are included.

What we can offer (summary):
• License boundary: we will add explicit license language that covers runtime images, compiled inference artifacts (including quantized weights), and config required to run inference. Training data, training checkpoints, and development source are explicitly excluded.
• Evidence & snapshot procedure: sealed, hash-signed read-only snapshot deliverable; delivery options: secure S3 or physical transfer; optional independent witness session. See attached Exhibit outline for details.
• Custody attestation: signed operator affidavit available within 5 business days of snapshot creation.
• Timelines: snapshot export 10 business days; witness session 15 business days; attestations 3–5 business days.

Requested from EdgeHealth: please confirm preferred contingency model (Option A: sealed snapshot deposit with third-party custodian, or Option B: witnessed transfer + acceptance runbook). Once you confirm, Rachel will produce a clean addendum redline and we can circulate for your counsel.

Call option: I have time Thursday 9–11 AM PT if you want to walk through this with counsel. Otherwise we'll produce the redline and DocuSign packet for procurement.
